title: Up a tree (Luke 19:1–10)
hookLine: a short, rich, hated man climbs a sycamore and Jesus invites himself to dinner
carry: today salvation came to this house

lines: A TAX BOSS, RICH, AND SHORT.
A GROWN MAN CLIMBS A TREE.
cards: Jericho. A crowd lines the street because Jesus is passing through. Somewhere at the back is a man named Zacchaeus.
Luke gives us three facts about him. He's the chief of the tax collectors there. He's rich.

And he's short. He wants to see Jesus, he can't see over anybody, and nobody is going to make room for him. So a grown man, wealthy and important, runs ahead down the road like a boy and climbs up into a sycamore tree.

teach.b: Jesus comes to the spot, looks up, and calls him by name. In the Douay-Rheims: "Zacheus, make haste and come down; for this day I must abide in thy house." He doesn't wait to be asked.
He invites himself, and not to just anyone's house: to the house of the man the crowd calls a sinner. Zacchaeus scrambles down and welcomes him with joy. The crowd does not.
Everyone grumbles: he's gone to stay with a sinner. Then Zacchaeus stands up and says something no one expected.
Look, Lord, half of what I own I'm giving to the poor, and if I've cheated anyone of anything, I'll pay it back four times over. Notice the order. Jesus didn't make him promise first.
He came to the house first.
The welcome came before the change, and the change came pouring out of the welcome.

teach.h: HALF TO THE POOR, FOUR TIMES BACK.
teach.b: Then Jesus says: "This day is salvation come to this house." And the line that sums up everything he's been doing on this road: "For the Son of man is come to seek and to save that which was lost."
The sheep, the coin, the son, all in one sentence.

teach.h: TODAY — THE ANGELS' WORD, AND HIS.
teach.b: One word ties it together: today. Luke used it at the birth, too: the angels say a savior is born to you this day.

teach.h: TO SEEK AND TO SAVE THAT WHICH WAS LOST.
teach.b: Now, in Jericho, today. Not someday, when you've fixed yourself. Today.
The Church reads this Gospel when a new church building is dedicated: a house where Christ has come to stay.

how: Catholics hear the story of Zacchaeus at Sunday Mass and at the Mass for the dedication of a church, and it is often preached as a picture of welcome leading to conversion and restitution.

games.q: you're Jesus, walking through Jericho. a rich, hated tax collector is up a tree to see you. what do you do?
o: walk on by. the crowd is watching.
call him down by name and say you're staying at his house.
tell him to give his money away first.
games.why: “Zacheus, make haste and come down; for this day I must abide in thy house.” the change comes after.

practice: Think of someone you've already made up your mind about: the difficult coworker, the neighbor with the loud truck, the relative who always says the wrong thing. You know what they're like, or you think you do.
Hold them in mind, remember Zacchaeus called by name before he'd changed at all, and ask whether this person could still surprise you. If you pray, you can pray for them by name.

wordCard.voice: Zacchaeus. The short, rich tax collector up a sycamore tree, called down by name and changed at his own table.

orig.note: Greek: today. The angels' word at the birth in Luke, and Jesus's word at this house in Jericho.

carryVoice: Your line: today salvation came to this house. The welcome came first. See you tomorrow.
